title: One Day on the Reef
theme: Four groups rotate through three hands-on experiences at John Pennekamp Coral Reef State Park, 9:00 AM to 2:30 PM.

blocks.title: Glass-Bottom Boat Tour
blocks.description: Students observe coral habitats and marine life from above on a glass-bottom boat excursion, pairing accessible reef viewing with guided interpretation. Groups C & D sail 9:00–11:30 AM; Groups A & B sail 12:15–2:30 PM.

blocks.title: Citizen Science & Fish ID
blocks.description: Students learn how REEF volunteers identify fish and collect survey data, building the skills needed to participate in citizen science and marine biodiversity monitoring. Groups A & B in the morning; Groups C & D in the afternoon.

blocks.title: Lionfish Lesson & Dissection
blocks.description: Students investigate invasive lionfish through a hands-on lesson and guided dissection, linking anatomy and adaptation to real conservation challenges in Florida Keys ecosystems. Groups A & B in the morning; Groups C & D in the afternoon.

blocks.title: Picnic Lunch at Pennekamp
blocks.description: Groups break for a packed picnic lunch at the park's picnic tables, staggered between rotations.

studentsWill: Observe living coral reef habitats and marine life from the glass-bottom boat (Observe).
Learn REEF's fish identification and survey methods used by citizen scientists (Identify).
Investigate invasive lionfish anatomy and adaptation through a guided dissection (Understand).
Connect what they see to REEF's ongoing reef conservation and invasive-species work (Connect to Conservation).
